The son will not prevail, because the owner and the landscaper effectively modified their agreement and thereby deprived the son of any rights he may have had. He was an intended donee beneficiary, but his rights had not vested: he learned of the contract only after the payee was changed, and he had not assented, sued, or relied before that change. Under the modern rule, the contracting parties may modify a third-party beneficiary’s rights until vesting.

CONFIDENCE: 86
